hints: Apply the factor theorem to both polynomials: $(x-2)$ being a factor means $p(2)=0$ and $p'(2)=0$.
Differentiate first, then substitute $x=2$ to obtain $12a-40+b=0$.
Solve these two linear equations simultaneously for $a$ and $b$.
walkthrough:
Apply the Factor Theorem to $p(x) = ax^3 - 10x^2 + bx + 8$ with factor $(x - 2)$:
$$p(2) = 0$$
$$a(2)^3 - 10(2)^2 + b(2) + 8 = 0$$
$$8a - 10(4) + 2b + 8 = 0$$
$$8a - 40 + 2b + 8 = 0$$
$$8a + 2b - 32 = 0$$
Divide through by $2$ to simplify:
$$4a + b = 16 \quad [\text{Equation 1}]$$

Differentiate $p(x)$ with respect to $x$ to find $p'(x)$:
$$p'(x) = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(ax^3 - 10x^2 + bx + 8) = 3ax^2 - 20x + b$$

Apply the Factor Theorem to $p'(x)$ with factor $(x - 2)$:
$$p'(2) = 0$$
$$3a(2)^2 - 20(2) + b = 0$$
$$3a(4) - 40 + b = 0$$
$$12a + b - 40 = 0$$
$$12a + b = 40 \quad [\text{Equation 2}]$$

Subtract [Equation 1] from [Equation 2] to eliminate $b$:
$$(12a + b) - (4a + b) = 40 - 16$$
$$8a = 24 \implies a = \dfrac{24}{8} = 3$$

Substitute $a = 3$ into [Equation 1] to solve for $b$:
$$4(3) + b = 16$$
$$12 + b = 16 \implies b = 16 - 12 = 4$$

hints: Use the values from part (a) to write $p(x)=3x^3-10x^2+4x+8$.
Because $(x-2)$ is a factor of both $p$ and $p'$, $x=2$ is a repeated root, so divide by $(x-2)^2$.
Factorise the remaining linear quotient and check that the leading and constant terms reproduce those of $p(x)$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the values $a = 3$ and $b = 4$ found in part (a) into $p(x)$:
$$p(x) = 3x^3 - 10x^2 + 4x + 8$$
Since $(x - 2)$ is a factor of both $p(x)$ and $p'(x)$, $x = 2$ is a repeated root of $p(x) = 0$, meaning $(x - 2)^2$ is a factor of $p(x)$.

Divide $p(x)$ by $(x - 2)$ using polynomial long division:
$$\dfrac{3x^3 - 10x^2 + 4x + 8}{x - 2}$$
Divide the leading term $3x^3$ by $x$: $3x^2$
Subtract $3x^2(x - 2) = 3x^3 - 6x^2$:
$$(3x^3 - 10x^2 + 4x + 8) - (3x^3 - 6x^2) = -4x^2 + 4x + 8$$
Divide $-4x^2$ by $x$: $-4x$
Subtract $-4x(x - 2) = -4x^2 + 8x$:
$$(-4x^2 + 4x + 8) - (-4x^2 + 8x) = -4x + 8$$
Divide $-4x$ by $x$: $-4$
Subtract $-4(x - 2) = -4x + 8$:
$$(-4x + 8) - (-4x + 8) = 0$$
Thus the quotient is $3x^2 - 4x - 4$:
$$p(x) = (x - 2)(3x^2 - 4x - 4)$$

Factorise the quadratic factor $3x^2 - 4x - 4$ by splitting the middle term:
Find two numbers with product $3 \times (-4) = -12$ and sum $-4$, which are $-6$ and $2$:
$$3x^2 - 6x + 2x - 4 = 3x(x - 2) + 2(x - 2) = (3x + 2)(x - 2)$$

Assemble all linear factors into the complete factorisation of $p(x)$:
$$p(x) = (x - 2)(3x + 2)(x - 2) = (3x + 2)(x - 2)^2$$
